```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(digits=2)
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
require(lubridate)
require(mosaic)
kRdata <- read.csv(file = 'kRdata.csv')
kRdata <- kRdata %>%
mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
kData = kRdata
```
Data are from the Patient_Info dataset from South Korea 1 Jan to 1 May 2020. These data were retrieved from a downloadable zip file from kaggle.

Some of the data were uncoded for sex - sex must be just male or female.  77 of the data entries were coded sex as blank, so we omit these.  State of a patient must be died or alive - we adjust that as well.  This is done in the mutate function. 

Variables of interest: sex, result

Research Question: - Is dying independent of sex?

# Introduction

Data from K Data. Question is: Is sex a factor of dying from Covid19?

$H_0$ : No, sex is not a factor of dying from Covid19. Males and females are equally likely to die of it.

$H_A$ : YES, sex is a factor of dying from Covid19.... Males and females may die at different rates from it! 

# Methods

Sex is categorical, result is also categorical. So we use the Cat~Cat helper file!!!!!

# Data Results

## Graphical results 

```{r}
barchartGC(~result + sex,data=kData)
barchartGC(~result + sex,data=kData, type="percent")

```
The graph suggests that males on average die more due to Covid compared to females!

## Numerical results

```{r}
table1 <- xtabs(~result + Sex, data=kData)
rowPerc(table1)
colPerc(table1)
```
From these results we can see that out of 100, 64% of dead Covid19 victims were male, and 36% were female. we can clearly deduce that males appear to have a higher death rate, being almost twice as likely to die!

## Inferential results 

```{r}
chisq.test(table1)
chisqtestGC(table1)
fisher.test(table1)
```
p value is 0.001 which is less than 0.05. So we can reject the null hypothesis and conclude that there is a connection between sex and dying of Covid19. 

# Conclusions

Original question: Is sex a factor of dying from Covid19?
